subject: Clio phase 100700 - entity-overlap match reason (display-only), developer r4 staged diff
verdict_justification: Every in-scope bullet of the phase has code plus test evidence, and I re-verified the claims myself instead of trusting the developer's summary: the full coverage gate exits 0 with all 352 files above the per-file floor, clippy and rustfmt are clean, and my own real-binary run against the built `clio` binary passes 17 checks including the dense leg the developer had listed as unverified. The one substantive weakness is that the derived label exists only in the human text view; the machine-readable payload that agents actually read carries a bare `entity_match: true` with nothing marking it as an inference. The remaining items are small: two test gaps against explicit acceptance conditions and one wrong line count in the phase's own evidence table.

findings.title: The machine-readable payload carries no derived marker; only the human text view labels the reason
findings.evidence: crates/clio-retrieve/src/types.rs:155-165 (field `entity_match: bool`, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")]`; the derived status lives only in the Rust doc comment) and crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_read_defs.rs:100-101 (the `retrieve` tool description is one line, 'Adaptive dense + lexical + optional graph retrieval.', and never mentions the field), against crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_render.rs:48 where the text view does print '[derived] entity match (display-only; not a ranking signal)'. Confirmed in my real-binary run: adversary-e2e.out.txt shows the JSON hit as "entities":["Grace Hopper"],"entity_match":true with nothing in the payload marking the second key as an inference.
findings.requirement_ref: Phase 100700 Goal ('the reason is labelled derived everywhere it appears'); Task 2 Required Change 1; section 10 failure mode 'Reason presented as verified'; requirement.md FR-4 / PR-4 (a span-verified value and an inferred overlap must not be confused)
findings.recommendation: Put the label where the machine reads it, not only in prose. Cheapest correct options: rename the key to `entity_match_derived`, add a sibling `"derived": true` on the hit, or extend the `retrieve` tool description in schema_read_defs.rs to say that `entity_match` is a derived, display-only inference and not a verification result. Keep `entities[]` and this field visually distinct in the payload so an agent cannot read the pair as a confirmed fact. The phase's Implementation Freedom allows a boolean representation, so this is a spec-reading gap in the labelling duty, not a code bug.

issues.title: The machine-readable payload carries no derived marker; only the human text view labels the reason
issues.why_it_matters: The phase's own goal sentence says the reason is 'labelled derived everywhere it appears', and its failure-mode table lists 'Reason presented as verified' as a defect to fix by adding the derived label. The label exists in exactly one place: the CLI text line. The MCP and in-process JSON payloads, which are what an agent actually reads, serialize a bare `entity_match: true` sitting next to `entities: [...]`, a value that FR-4 span-verifies at write time. Nothing inside the payload tells the reader which of the two keys is an inference. An agent that trusts the payload can report 'the store confirmed the entity matched the query', which is the exact claim the phase exists to prevent.
issues.impact: Fidelity risk on the primary consumption path. The human CLI user is protected; a programmatic consumer is not. The phase's Implementation Freedom does permit a boolean flag, so this is a duty to label that was met only in prose, not a wrong implementation.
issues.confidence: High - verified by reading the serializer, the tool schema, and a real payload.
issues.proposed_fix: Carry the label in the payload the agent reads: rename the key to `entity_match_derived`, or add a sibling `"derived": true`, or extend the `retrieve` tool description to state that `entity_match` is a derived display-only inference and never a verification result. Any of the three closes the gap without changing the rule, the ranking, or the payload's false-omission behaviour.

issues.title: Health and telemetry are named in the security acceptance condition but have no in-repo test for the reason
issues.why_it_matters: Task 2 Required Change 3 and section 7 both list four surfaces: warnings, explain trace, telemetry, health. The new boundary test covers two of them. The other two are argued structurally (no sink serializes a hit) rather than pinned by a test, so a future change that starts projecting per-hit data into a health or telemetry surface would not be caught by the reason-specific test.
issues.impact: Test-coverage gap against an explicit acceptance condition. No live leak: runtime_sinks.rs:178-181 reduces hits to item_id, and my real-binary run found no `entity_match` and no entity name in `ops diagnose` or `ops verify`.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/read_entities_tests.rs:341-397 (two surfaces), :238-278 (health sweep pins names only); crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime_sinks.rs:178-181; adversary-e2e.out.txt.
issues.proposed_fix: Extend the health sweep to assert the reason key alongside the names, and note in the test or module header that no telemetry sink receives per-hit data, so the omission reads as deliberate.

issues.title: Dense-leg flag untested in-repo while the fixture for it already exists
issues.why_it_matters: The developer listed the dense leg as a verification limit. The same crate already has the exact fixture needed (a vector-only item plus a fixed embedder) used to prove the sibling `entities` field is leg-independent. Leaving the new flag untested there means leg independence rests on code reading plus a private script that no future run will execute.

issues.evidence: crates/clio-retrieve/src/hit_entities_tests.rs:128-158 (the pattern to mirror); phase Completion Evidence 'Verification limits'; adversary-e2e.out.txt (dense_rank=1 with entity_match=true).
issues.proposed_fix: Mirror the existing dense test in entity_match_tests.rs, asserting entity_match on a hit that has dense_rank set and a semantic score.

dismissed: Substring containment matching a name inside a longer token ('art' in 'restart'). Documented in three places (entity_match.rs:26-33, docs/recall-entity-match.md, phase Known Limitations) and pinned by a test. It is a documented design choice, not a defect.

Full Unicode case folding is not used, so 'ß' does not match 'SS'. Verified as a real stdlib limit: str::to_lowercase is the stable mapping and the case-folding API is unstable, so no dependency-free fix exists. Documented and tested.

The three clio-mcp test-file edits (ops_tools_tests.rs, read_dedup_tests.rs, read_scores_tests.rs) are outside this phase's behaviour. Not a finding: the earlier blocked attempt requested them as an explicit unblock, the resume notice listed them as existing tree state, they touch no production file, and they harden test doubles rather than weaken assertions.

No committed end-to-end test at process level. The E2E evidence is a run-artifact script, but the in-repo CLI test pins the exact rendered line and I reproduced the binary run independently, so nothing is unpinned.
`#[serde(default)]` on entity_match is inert because ScoredHit derives only Serialize. It matches the existing convention on entities/consolidated/source_ids, so it is consistency, not error.
docs/recall-scope-and-dedup.md:35 still describes the always-present per-hit fields as scores and entities. Still true, since entity_match is omitted when false; updating it would be optional polish.

strengths: The rule lives in one 96-line pure function pair with its normalization and its limits documented in the module header, so there is exactly one place to change the match behaviour.
The flag is computed once in the retrieval layer and projected by serde, so JSON and text cannot disagree by construction; the render helper only formats a value it is handed.
The payload convention is right: the key is omitted when false, so a non-matching hit keeps exactly the shape it had before the field existed, and a test pins that.
The false-positive behaviour of substring matching is documented instead of hidden, with a test that names the consequence ('art' inside 'restart').
The decision record explains why display-only was chosen and lists what a future rank-based leg would need, which is what the phase asked for and more than most phases deliver.

Coverage and size discipline held: every touched file is at or below 450 lines, the new module is at 100% function and line coverage, and the derived label is asserted against leaks of the entity name in three separate tests plus the real binary.
regrets: The phase asked for a reason that is labelled derived everywhere it appears, and the implementer read that as satisfied by the text label plus documentation. The machine payload is where the risk actually lives.
The dense-leg test was left as a documented limitation when the fixture for it was already in the same crate, used for the sibling field.
process_changes: When a phase names a labelling duty, check every surface the value reaches, not only the one the phase's Implementation Freedom paragraph mentions first.
When a phase lists surfaces in a security acceptance condition, treat each named surface as needing its own assertion, even when the current architecture makes a leak impossible.
Re-run the developer's real-binary script only as a cross-check; write an independent one, because that is what found the dense-leg evidence the phase file lacked.

Close issue 2: extend the health-surface sweep to assert the reason key as well as the names, and say in the test that no telemetry sink receives per-hit data.
Close issue 3: mirror hit_entities_tests.rs:128-158 in entity_match_tests.rs to pin the flag on a dense-leg hit.

plan_unlimited: Design and validate a rank-based entity leg as its own phase: a fusion weight measured against the benchmark harness, plus an explicit decision on boost versus filter, referencing the display-only decision record rather than retrofitting ranking into this flag.
Add word-boundary matching as a documented option next to plain containment, and measure how often each fires on real queries before changing the default.
